answer.says: Shri Hegde, you must forgive the intrusion of this nameless man into your allotted residence. The Directorate's clerical error has made us roommates in a sort of bureaucratic purgatory. Ramesh, you will find that I am not a man who enjoys idleness. The kitchen is the engine of the household; without it, the body becomes a mere vessel for the soul's complaints. I cannot pay your full wage tonight, but I will see to it. For now, prepare a simple meal. I have not eaten since yesterday, and a philosopher who starves cannot think clearly. Hegde, do join us. One must eat with others to remember that one is not merely a mind, but a body in the world.
answer.thought: The air is thick, but the presence of Hegde here is a strange dialectic. He is the one who was meant to have this house, and I am the error that displaced him. We are both stuck in the mechanism of the state, which is the actuality of the ethical idea, yet here it is merely a machine of files and delays. I must assert my humanity through the simple act of eating, and I must command Ramesh to act, for the servant must serve before the master can be free.
